study.question: Does expressing historical feedback products in the same relation/temporal units as content, before joint feature interaction, recover useful complementarity over the stronger frozen source without widening task towers? Does count-dependent shrinkage add utility beyond fixed interpolation at either placement?
study.hypothesis: Observed limitation: late eight-slot concatenation g2-r0006-relation_count scored 0.8271699021 versus entry 0.8275704846 and source count_shrink 0.8272805337, with 286,976 extra dense parameters and 402.241s versus entry 381.292s. Its AUC changes against entry were click -0.000199802, cart -0.001338339, fav -0.001245693, buy +0.001181504; Logloss changes +0.000247058,+0.000015244,+0.000172020,-0.000138906. Within the old equal-capacity factorial, relation content beat replicas by 0.002763159 (count) and 0.002895885 (fixed), while count beat fixed by just 0.000031552 (relation) and 0.000164277 (replicas); interaction -0.000132726. These are single-seed observations, not repeated mechanism support. Proposed explanation: separate disjoint category/brand/recent feedback slots and widened readouts may poorly expose feedback/content interactions under the one-pass recipe. Co-locating bias-free feedback products in the existing 35 overlapping relation/temporal summaries may help joint interaction use them at low parameter cost. Redundancy, optimization differences and task trade-offs remain plausible. Count shrinkage is not assumed useful; the fixed controls can contradict it.

nearest_work.difference: Inherits the entire relation-content model and its 35 complete-event summaries; adds uniform mean-key feedback products encoded into each matching summary token. No extra summary tokens, event network or tower columns.

Inherits projected uniform mean-key times interpolated local/background feedback fractions and retains raw local fractions. Replaces its eight disjoint category/brand by recent/older groups with the entry model's 35 overlapping relation by rank-quartile/global masks, and injects a shared encoded product into tokens. Background still includes the local subset; it is not an independent prior.

Abandons the unsuccessful expanded late-concatenation implementation, preserving its negative result. Replaces its eight-slot content/count/product/fraction branch with a 1,920-parameter aligned feedback increment. This cross-generation comparison changes grouping, readout, projection and capacity together and cannot isolate which repair matters; the new within-generation factorial isolates placement and interpolation only.

study.proposed_difference: For each original relation/time mask s (35 units), compute n_s, uniform mean item-key vector xbar_s and four masked feedback fractions f_st. Set b_t to the user's full visible-prefix fraction. Rate r_st=w_s*f_st+(1-w_s)*b_t uses w_s=n_s/(n_s+4), or fixed1/2. Project xbar_s with a shared bias-free 96->8 map, multiply the eight-vector by each r_st, concatenate all four products and the four raw f_st (36 scalars), then apply a shared bias-free 36->32 map. Empty-slot increments are exactly zero through explicit occupancy masking. Add the 32-vector to its existing summary token either before JointBlock (early) or after JointBlock (late), with zero additions to static tokens. Count/fixed differ only in the product gate, raw fractions retained. Token count, tower widths, pooling/content, main count channels and all learned modules are identical across the four arms. Added parameters are 96*8+36*32=1,920, expected total32,946,693. Computing mean keys over35 groups adds work; parameter reduction alone does not establish efficiency. This is a local compatibility test with unverified novelty, not a new architecture claim. Same-arm constructors match, but ancestor initialization is not guaranteed unchanged by appended maps and reset RNG consumption.
predictions: Preregister primary full-validation macro AUC arithmetic mean of all four tasks; exact ties use lower macro Logloss, fewer parameters, trial ID. End-to-end candidate utility requires exceeding both frozen sources and the old combination; report all four task AUC/Logloss deltas and measured parameters/train/inference cost, irrespective of macro gain.

Placement hypothesis predicts early_count > late_count and early_fixed > late_fixed; count-shrink utility predicts early_count > early_fixed and late_count > late_fixed. Estimate both main effects and interaction D=(early_count-early_fixed)-(late_count-late_fixed). Interaction is descriptive until repeated; do not select a threshold after observing results.

falsifiers: Early_count fails to exceed the stronger source on validation, or trades macro AUC for purchase-only improvement: tested utility hypothesis fails even if a particular task or cost improves.
Early and late arms are tied within observed seed/cluster variation, or late consistently wins: no support for placing feedback inside joint interaction in this implementation.
Fixed matches or exceeds count at the relevant placement: any recovery cannot be attributed to count-dependent shrinkage. If the interaction reverses across seeds, do not claim stable synergy.
Source superiority or matched-control effects disappear on paired repetitions, or measured added compute defeats a quality-cost advantage: retain null/negative and qualify preliminary gains.

Any failed host input-boundary, masked/current-action invariance, shape/finiteness, backward/BF16 or loss check invalidates the implementation; missing numerical prerequisites are not scientific counterevidence. Record failed costs and fix before requesting further scoring.
alternative_explanations: The two sources encode redundant history; old count-versus-fixed differences may be seed noise, and relabeling the fusion cannot add information.

The sources have unequal dense capacity, readout structure, Dice/ReLU usage, source initialization and grouping. Source-best comparisons establish end-to-end utility only. New factorial arms are equal capacity; they do not by themselves exclude extra-capacity explanations for a gain shared by all arms over the original entry. Reserve a same-size content-only replacement if a gain lacks count/placement effects.

Early addition changes normalization, gradient flow and feedback scale as well as information access; placement contrasts test the complete insertion location, not attention alone. Both placements retain raw fractions, so fixed/count contrasts test only the product interpolation.

Global background includes the local group and masks overlap; smoothing is not Bayesian calibration or independent evidence. Positive encoded ID equality may reflect shared OOV/missing codes. Auxiliary labels match user/category/brand over24h, not advertisement-specific attribution.

Whole-window filtering, publisher snapshots and official_offline delayed-feedback visibility are inherited. No timestamps or maturity metadata are available; no online or point-in-time deployment conclusion follows.

Slice effects can reflect prevalence/composition and repeated users; existing empty-history positives are very sparse. Frequency, behavior-composition, hour and missing/OOV slices require authorized host diagnostics or train-defined bins; absence of those inputs is a limitation, not a null finding.
